sentence: This project studies whether heart artery patients who had COVID-19 infection have more inflammation and faster plaque growth in their coronary arteries.
This project studies how a gene that is critical for memory forms virus-like capsids that move proteins and RNA between cells.
This project builds a cancer metastasis model with tissue engineering that reflects organ-specificity, and tests it using kidney cancer.
This project builds a method to measure emerging Fusarium and Alternaria mycotoxins accurately in pet food and livestock feed.
This project builds mass spectrometry-based tools that give structural information about complex biological systems such as protein-DNA complexes.
This project studies how cadherin cell recognition molecules help wire connections between the mouse retina and superior colliculus.
This project supplies viral stocks and sequencing for rat and mouse models of infection to test whether designed vaccines protect against different viral variants.
This project studies how cocaine-sensitive variants of a dopamine receptor gene affect cocaine-seeking and taking behavior in preclinical models.
This project tries to find out whether some people gather mutations faster or slower with age and whether that predicts how long they live.
This project builds an interactive guide that helps kidney patients on hemodialysis choose a vascular access type, using a model that predicts outcomes.
This project builds tools to study how cells use microvesicles to communicate with each other.
This project builds methods to track single cells and their fate in space as they adapt to stress, including how cancer cells resist therapy.
This project tries to find out how tubulin modifications and a small GTPase protein affect the health of light-sensing photoreceptor cells.
This project tests agents and drug combinations in preclinical models of pediatric high-risk sarcoma, liver, and kidney cancers.
This project builds algorithms and software that help reuse publicly available RNA sequencing data so cancer researchers can form better ideas about tumors.
This project studies how mutant blood cells in clonal hematopoiesis send inflammation signals to other cells and make plaques less stable.
This project studies how genes control temporal patterning in retinal progenitor cells and whether retinal glial cells can be reprogrammed into progenitor cells.
This project studies how signaling molecules work together in neurons of the inferior colliculus to shape sound processing.
This project studies how obesity early in life changes T cells and weakens T follicular helper cells, which regulate immune responses.
This project tests whether an antibody against a bone cell receptor can improve bone strength and fracture healing in a preclinical spinal cord injury model.
